experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: A classic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Given the late Day 1 arrival, begin trekking on Day 2 after a proper rest and early morning preparation in Pokhara. The trail passes through rhododendron forests, traditional Gurung villages, and dramatic mountain scenery culminating in a 360-degree view of the Annapurna massif. Allocate 7-9 days for the full round trip.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Viewpoint Hike
experiences.description: Trek to Poon Hill (3,210m) for one of the most iconic Himalayan sunrises, with panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Machhapuchhre. Since Day 1 is lost to a late arrival, use Day 2 to travel to Nayapul and begin the ascent toward Ghorepani, reaching Poon Hill on Day 3 at dawn. A manageable and rewarding short trek within the 14-day window.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: A less-crowded alternative trek leading to Mardi Himal Base Camp at 4,500m, offering stunning close-up views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain). Start on Day 2 from Pokhara after resting from the late arrival. The 5-6 day trail winds through dense forests and high alpine meadows, ideal for nature lovers seeking solitude away from the main Annapurna circuit crowds.

experiences.name: Pokhara Lakeside Nature Walk and Kayaking
experiences.description: Use the evening of Day 1 (post late arrival) and the morning of Day 2 wisely with a gentle lakeside walk along Phewa Lake followed by a kayaking session at sunrise. This low-intensity activity allows acclimatization and recovery before the main treks begin, while offering stunning reflections of the Annapurna range on the lake. Kayak rentals are affordable and widely available.

experiences.name: Annapurna Circuit Highlights: Manang Valley Acclimatization Hike
experiences.description: If incorporating part of the Annapurna Circuit, spend an acclimatization day hiking above Manang village to Ice Lake (4,600m) or Gangapurna Lake. This is best scheduled mid-trek to prevent altitude sickness before crossing Thorong La Pass. With a Day 2 trek start (accounting for the late Day 1 arrival), this fits naturally into a 14-day itinerary covering the circuit highlights.
